resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy for Change in Occupancy (Certificate of Continued Occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Elsinboro Township Housing and Zoning Officer
requirements: Home may not be occupied until the Housing/Zoning Officer issues a certificate of occupancy
Water test (NJDEP and federal EPA chemical, bacteriological and gross alpha limits); not needed on a public water system
Chimney certification for all fossil fuel systems
Smoke detectors (each level, including the top of the basement stairs and a heated garage) and carbon monoxide alarms near bedrooms
Electrical panel labeled, 100 amp service or more
GFCI outlets in kitchen, bathrooms, laundry, garage and outside
Handrails on basement, porch and deck steps; emergency heater switch at the top of the stairs; heater serviced and inspected
Water heater relief pipe piped down
Roof, siding, windows, doors and screens in good repair; house numbered; trash, debris and abandoned vehicles removed
Fire-resistant door and walls between an attached garage and the house
Fire extinguisher (2A:10B:C) listed on the Township instructions, which predate P.L.2025, c.19

fees.label: Certificate of occupancy (change in occupancy) inspection

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Township's Application for Certificate of Occupancy for Change in Occupancy (property, current owner, buyer, both realtors, type of dwelling and rooms) and have the seller's realtor or owner sign it. The application is not complete until the owner or realtor calls the Housing/Zoning Officer at 935-2200 to schedule the inspection. Zoning and housing hours are Thursday 3pm to 4pm (construction hours are now Wednesday 4:30pm to 6:00pm) at the Municipal Building, 619 Salem Ft-Elfsborg Rd, Salem.
resale_co.contact_title: Zoning and Housing Official (also Construction and Building Subcode Official)

resale_co.notes: The Departments page now names Andy Hoglen under 'Construction, Zoning and Housing' (inspector@elsinborotownship.com), matching the 2026 reorganization minutes, and construction hours moved to Wednesday 4:30pm to 6:00pm; zoning and housing hours are still Thursday 3pm to 4pm. The CO Application on the Forms page is the same file as before. This time Township Code Chapter 145, Occupancy Certificates (Ord. No. 77-9 of 11-7-1977), was read through the ecode360 print view: §145-1 says a buyer may not occupy a dwelling unit, or let others occupy it, without first getting a certificate of occupancy from the Township Housing Officer, and §145-2 requires compliance with all Township building, plumbing, electrical, zoning, health, fire and housing ordinances. §145-4 (Ord. 2022-04) adds lead-based paint rules for rentals and says no CO for a home built before 1979 can be issued without a lead-safe or lead-free certificate; the section is written about rental units, so whether it applies to an owner-occupied sale is unclear. Chapter 68 (Fees) lists no certificate of occupancy fee; the $30.00 inspection and $30.00 reinspection fees come from the application form. The application form is a scanned PDF with no text layer, read visually. It is undated and bundles a 2005 DCA memo on fire extinguishers. The instructions page has handwritten notes ('Deleted' next to the septic certification, '2A10BC' next to the extinguisher); handwritten notes are weak evidence, so septic is left out of requirements and the extinguisher is flagged as predating P.L.2025, c.19 (February 3, 2025). No direct phone for the Housing Officer is listed; the Township's main number 856-935-2200 is the scheduling number on the form, and the Officials page lists 'Building Inspector/Zoning Officer 856-935-2200'. No lead time or validity period is stated.

Ask the Township who issues the certificate; the DCA Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement can confirm.

fire_cert.notes: Who issues the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate in Elsinboro is not settled. The State (NJ DCA) is the fire code enforcing agency (registry code S; state directory code 1703), and the state directory lists 'NJ Division Fire Safety' under smoke detector compliance. But the DCA's state towns list (revised 7/17/2026) shows Elsinboro without the 'SC' (State issues smoke certs) mark, and the DCA portal data marks ELSINBORO TWP-001 as smoke-certificate exempt, the same flags seen in towns where the municipality issues the certificate itself. The Township's own certificate of occupancy checks smoke detectors and carbon monoxide alarms, and under N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3(a)1 a municipal resale inspection can stand in for the separate certificate, but no Township page says so. No fees are recorded for either authority until this is confirmed. The Elsinboro Fire Company (Chief Sean Elwell) is the volunteer fire company, not an inspecting agency. The DCA's online smoke application loads its town list from the same portal data feed; towns marked smoke-certificate exempt, as this one is, are not offered there, so the State's online route should not be given to agents for this town.

other_items.label: Water test
other_items.detail: A water test (NJDEP and federal EPA chemical, bacteriological and gross alpha limits) must be provided before the certificate is issued, unless the home is on a public water system.

other_items.label: Chimney certification
other_items.detail: Required for all fossil fuel systems; the visual inspection can be done by a heating contractor or chimney sweep.

other_items.label: Lead-safe or lead-free certificate (pre-1979 homes, rental rule)
other_items.detail: Township Code §145-4 says no certificate of occupancy for a home built before 1979 can be issued without a lead-safe or lead-free certificate from a state-licensed lead inspector. The section is written for rental units under P.L.2021, c.182; ask whether the Township applies it to owner-occupied sales.

open_questions: Who issues the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate for Elsinboro: the Township Housing/Zoning Officer as part of the certificate of occupancy, or the NJ DCA? What is the fee?
Is the septic certification still required (it is crossed out by hand as 'Deleted' on the instructions page)?
Does the Township apply the §145-4 lead-safe or lead-free certificate rule to owner-occupied sales of pre-1979 homes, or only to rentals?
Does the Township still check for a fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19?
How far ahead of closing should the certificate of occupancy be requested, and how long is it valid?
